transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 PST | Duration ~62m | Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood SRE); Dana Ortiz (Nimbus CTO), Marcus Li (ML Platform), Sofia Perez (Infra)

[00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll try to keep this focused on the OOMs and cuda timeouts you reported. quick intro, I'm Liam, AE. Priya is our runtime SE and Noah is our SRE who runs the private deployments.
[00:12] Dana Ortiz: Thanks Liam. we'll mostly be talking about an on-prem cluster, 8x A100-ish nodes, mixed workloads, and some models quantized to 4-bit. seeing OOMs during bursts and occasionally these cuda driver timeouts which kill the process.
[00:27] Priya Raman: ok thanks. Marcus, can you quickly recap the repro pattern — is it warm model traffic, cold start, or big batches?
[00:35] Marcus Li: it's mostly during sustained traffic spikes when KV cache hit rates are lower — prefix caching helps but when we hit longer seq lengths and some long-poll requests it spikes. we see OOMs on the host VM that correspond to the worker that held large KV state. sometimes timeouts show up when a different job tries to evict and kernel hangs, maybe driver-level.
[00:55] Sofia Perez: to add, we use a VPC-connected private control plane, and our k8s autoscaler has aggressive scale-down which might be preempting hot pods, causing cold starts. also we've got a custom sidecar for metrics which increases memory slightly.
[01:12] Priya Raman: that gives useful context. couple of initial hypotheses: 1) KV cache memory accounting vs container limits mismatch 2) batching/backpressure not effectively limiting sequence-length heavy requests 3) kernel/driver mismatch leading to cuda timeouts during eviction or heavy concat ops.
[01:34] Dana Ortiz: For KV cache memory accounting, is Redwood's default cache kept in GPU or host mem? we thought it was on GPU but docs said hybrid.
[01:43] Noah Kim: currently our runtime supports both. by default KV is in GPU with a host spillover for large caches. but on private deployments the config can be toggled. if you hit host memory limits we also see oom_killer events.
[01:58] Marcus Li: our helm set had cache.store=auto which I guess picked GPU-first. could host spillover be disabled? we didn't set explicit host limits so pods can be OOMed by k8s.
[02:09] Priya Raman: yes if host spill is disabled and GPU-held KV grows beyond GPU memory, you'd hit OOMs on the GPU process. That normally raises CUDA OOM errors; but a driver timeout often appears when the GPU is blocked waiting on a long synchronous op.
[02:28] Liam Carter: quick interruption — can you paste the exact error from your logs? we had your sample earlier but want to see timestamped sequence.
[02:36] Marcus Li: sure here's an excerpt we sent: "E tensorflow: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory" then later "E runtime: gpu kernel launch timed out - killing process". sometimes the process restarts and later shows "KV miss surge: from 10% to 60% -> fallback to full forward".
[02:55] Priya Raman: ok that aligns with hitting a large sequence workload that forces more KV allocation and spiky batching. two angles to explore: reduce max batch size and add per-request seq-length guards, and revisit KV eviction policy so we don't keep huge KV for cold prefixes.
[03:12] Sofia Perez: we've already tried lowering maxBatch to 8 but then latency jumps and we see timeouts upstream. we'd prefer a solution that avoids severe latency regressions.
[03:22] Priya Raman: understood; another tactic is dynamic batching with priority for low-latency requests and separate batch pools for long-seq jobs — that lets you keep small p99 for standard traffic while isolating heavy calls. our Dedicated product supports multi-pool routing but in private you can configure separate deployment classes.
[03:42] Dana Ortiz: is that the smart routing thing? we run a single pool atm. can we tag routes and have rules?
[03:49] Liam Carter: yes - route tags and policy-based routing. for now though, simple config change is to add a second deployment for long-seq/experimental models and pin those to a dedicated node pool.
[04:02] Marcus Li: ok will consider. about cuda timeouts specifically, could driver version mismatch cause kernel stalls during quantized matmul? we run CUDA 12.2 with cuDNN 9.2 but I think some kernels are new.
[04:14] Priya Raman: driver/kernel mismatches are a common cause. also some quantization paths (we saw with 4-bit QAT or PTQ) use fused kernels that are sensitive. we'll need to check the exact kernel names in your logs; sometimes a fallback to slower but stable kernels avoids timeouts.
[04:32] Noah Kim: Redwood's runtime has a kernel selector that prefers fast fused kernels; if you set runtime.kernel_selection=conservative in config it selects more stable kernels. tradeoff is throughput.
[04:44] Dana Ortiz: is there an automated canary for kernel selection? we'd rather not flip config blindly in prod.
[04:50] Priya Raman: we can run a canary on a small subset — that's a recommended step. Noah can help shard traffic and measure regressions.
[04:58] Noah Kim: yes. we can also enable verbose kernel logs for one node to capture exact launches.
[05:05] [05:05] Marcus Li: about retry semantics — currently our orchestration retries on 500s which sometimes causes cascading load as retries requeue and increase KV pressure. any best practices?
[05:14] Priya Raman: exponential backoff with jitter and rate-limiting on client-side is critical. on server side, we support idempotency keys and a short-lived local cache to avoid full recompute for retries within X seconds. also recommend adjusting retries to only retriable errors (connection resets) and not GPU OOMs which should fail fast.
[05:33] Liam Carter: to add, our recommended default retry policy is 3 tries with 200-800ms backoff for interactive workloads; for larger batch jobs we suggest 0-1 retries and longer timeouts.
[05:45] Marcus Li: sounds sensible. we'll probably change our retry filter.
[05:49] Sofia Perez: about k8s node autoscaler — could aggressive scale down cause in-flight KV invalidation and timeouts? we suspect pod churn correlates with incidents.
[05:59] Priya Raman: yes cold starts lead to cache misses and more work on backend. also if the autoscaler preempts a hot node running KV-heavy pods, the redistributed requests increase memory pressure elsewhere. configure scale-down grace periods and prefer cordon/drain sequencing that respects in-flight requests.
[06:18] Dana Ortiz: is there a suggested memory limit we should set on pods if KV is gpu-first? we currently leave limits open.
[06:25] Priya Raman: set explicit host and container memory limits; for GPU-first KV consider a GPU memory quota and host spill target. we often recommend pod hostMemoryLimit = modelSize*1.2 + kvBudget and set oomScoreAdj to protect the runtime.
[06:40] Marcus Li: can you share the exact formula or a playbook?
[06:44] Priya Raman: yes we'll share the quant/kernel/kv playbook — includes heuristics and examples for 7B/13B models, quantization settings and expected memory curves.
[06:55] Liam Carter: quick recap of agreed triage path: customer to provide full tracer logs incl kernel names, driver versions, helm values, and sample requests. Redwood to repro and run conservative kernel selection canary, try host spill config and adjust batching limits.
[07:09] Marcus Li: we can provide traces and a pcap of one incident, plus prometheus metrics around kube events.
[07:17] Noah Kim: we'll also capture node-level dmesg and nvidia-smi logs.
[07:22] Dana Ortiz: what about urgent mitigations we can do today? we're getting paged.
[07:27] Priya Raman: short term: 1) reduce concurrent max in your client, 2) lower maxBatch for long-seq routes, 3) enable conservative kernel selection, 4) increase scale-down grace period to avoid cold churn. all of these are non-invasive.
[07:43] Sofia Perez: can you give concrete commands for kernel selection toggle?
[07:47] Priya Raman: yes, we'll send exact helm/values snippet. e.g. runtime.kernel_selection: conservative and runtime.kv.spill_to_host: true (with hostMemoryLimit set).
[07:59] [07:59] Dana Ortiz: ok thanks. any comments on quantization tradeoffs? we loved the cost gains but worried about stability.
[08:07] Priya Raman: quantization often reduces memory but can change compute patterns — some fused int8/4 kernels are extremely fast but may trigger edge-case driver bugs. conservative approach: test PTQ then run stress tests under canary; consider per-op fallback to float for ops known to be flaky.
[08:27] Marcus Li: do you have a checklist for canarying quantized models?
[08:30] Priya Raman: yes, we'll include that in the playbook. checklist includes basic perf curves, long-running soak tests, kernel launch logs, and sample failure regimens.
[08:39] Liam Carter: we're at about 60 minutes so last quick recap and owners.
[08:44] Priya Raman: action items: I'll triage the trace and try repro; Noah will collect verbose kernel logs from our infra; Marcus will send helm values & driver versions; Redwood will send playbook and helm snippets and propose follow-up time.
[08:58] Dana Ortiz: thanks everyone, appreciate practical steps.
[09:03] Liam Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing with links.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker labels may be off (we heard speaker overlap), some punctuation cleaned for readability.
